## Abstract

<p class="abstract-text">Based on the data of the United Nations Commodity Trade Database from 2019 to 2021, this paper uses the social network analysis method to analyze the temporal and spatial pattern evolution of the global trade network under the influence of the COVID-19 epidemic. Research has found that ① There are significant regional differences in trade connections, with North America, Western Europe, and East Asia presenting a "three legged" pattern. ② The United States occupies a core position in the global trade network. The COVID-19 epidemic has reduced the scale of the global trade network and increasingly scattered network connections. ③ China, the United States and Germany are the core countries in the global commodity trade network. The COVID-19 epidemic has different impacts on different types of product trade and countries in different regions. ④ Economy, population, geographical distance, culture, and national policies have varying degrees of impact on global trade.</p>
